_why: Narration is decided twice: parseMessage.ts tints it on screen, speech_prep.py hands it to the engine. Two implementations in two languages will drift, and the drift is invisible - the screen italicises a span the ear hears in the character's own voice, or the reverse. This table is the single agreed answer. Both suites assert against it, so a divergence fails a test instead of surprising someone mid-conversation.
_shape: text = input. em = the substrings that must come out marked as narration, in order. If em is empty the text contains no narration at all.

cases.name: plain prose has no narration
cases.text: She looked at me and smiled.

cases.name: a single asterisk span is narration
triple run is both, so it counts as narration
arithmetic is not narration - a digit before the run blocks opening
mid-word asterisks do not open - a letter before the run blocks it
a run followed by whitespace does not open
cases.text: Look at that * thing over there.

cases.name: two narration spans in one reply
a blank line force-closes an unterminated span
cases.text:
*She turns away

and the room is quiet.

cases.name: an unclosed span runs to the end of the text
four or more asterisks are a decorative divider, not a delimiter
narration wrapping quoted speech keeps the quotes inside it
